item.title: How to Lower Your Electric Bill: The Complete Guide (2026)
item.description:
Quick Answer

You can cut your electric bill 20–40% with the highest-ROI moves: raise summer AC to 78°F (or drop winter heat to 68°F) saving $100–$300/year, switch to LEDs ($75/year), lower the water heater to 120°F ($40–$80/year), seal air leaks ($60–$200/year), shift laundry and dishwashing to off-peak hours, and kill vampire loads with smart strips ($50–$180/year).

  • Heating and cooling drive 40–50% of home energy costs — start there.
  • Most utilities run a free home energy audit; call before you spend a dollar.

Your electric bill is too high. You’ve tried turning off lights, but it barely made a dent. You want real savings—$50, $100, even $150 per month—and you want to know exactly what to do and what it’ll cost.

item.title: Phantom Power Draw: How to Find and Stop Silent Electricity Thieves
item.description:

Quick Answer

Phantom power (also called standby power or vampire draw) is electricity consumed by devices that are plugged in but turned off or in standby mode. It costs the average U.S. household $100–$200 per year — typically 5–10% of your total electric bill.

item.title: AC Short Cycling — Causes and Fixes
item.description:
Quick Answer

AC short cycling typically costs homeowners an extra $200-500 per season in wasted energy and premature system wear. Common causes include an oversized AC unit, dirty air filters, low refrigerant, or a malfunctioning thermostat.

  • A short-cycling AC unit can increase your energy bill by 15-30%
  • Check your air filter first—it’s the most common cause

[For more detail, see our complete guide to AC maintenance tips.]

Your air conditioner kicks on, runs for two minutes, shuts off, then starts again three minutes later. This pattern—called short cycling—is one of the most common and damaging HVAC problems homeowners face. It drives up your electricity bill, wears out your compressor prematurely, and leaves your home humid and uncomfortable. Here’s what causes it and how to fix each issue.
